The manufacturer must document a system to assign unique device identification to the medical device in accordance with the requirements of part 830 of this chapter, if applicable, and procedures for traceability in accordance with the requirements of part 821 of this chapter, if applicable, and notify FDA of complaints that meet the reporting criteria of part 803 of this chapter. Advisory notices shall be handled in accordance with the requirements of part 806 of this chapter. The requirements in Design and Development apply to class II, class III, and those class I devices listed in paragraph (c)(1) of this section and table 1 to paragraph (c)(2) of this section. Devices automated with computer software must comply with the requirements in Design and Development, Clause 7.3 and its Subclauses in ISO 13485. The devices listed in the following table must comply with the requirements in Design and Development, Clause 7.3 and its Subclauses in ISO 13485. Devices that support or sustain life must comply with the requirements in Traceability for Implantable Devices, Clause 7.5.9.2 in ISO 13485, in addition to all other applicable requirements in this part, as appropriate. The failure to comply with any applicable requirement in this part renders a device adulterated under section 501(h) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Such a device, as well as any person responsible for the failure to comply, is subject to regulatory action. [4][5]

A manufacturer subject to this part as described by § 820.1(a) must: Document a quality management system that complies with the applicable requirements of ISO 13485 (incorporated by reference, see § 820.7).

For Clause 7.5.8 in ISO 13485, Identification, the manufacturer must document a system to assign unique device identification to the medical device in accordance with the requirements of part 830 of this chapter.

raw_model_output:
What is Part 821?

Part 821 is a regulation under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (the act) that implements section 519(e) of the act. A device that meets one of the three criteria and is the subject of an FDA order must comply with this part and is referred to, in this part, as a “tracked device.” A manufacturer of a tracked device shall adopt a method of tracking for each such type of device that it distributes that enables a manufacturer to provide FDA with the following information in writing for each tracked device distributed. A distributor, final distributor, or multiple distributor of any tracked device shall, upon purchasing or otherwise acquiring any interest in such a device, promptly provide the manufacturer tracking the device with the information. The following definitions and terms apply to this part: the importer of a tracked device shall be considered the manufacturer and shall be required to comply with all requirements of this part applicable to manufacturers. Importers must keep all information required under this part in the United States. Manufacturers, distributors, multiple distributors, and final distributors shall, upon the presentation by an FDA representative of official credentials and the issuance of Form FDA 482 at the initiation of an inspection of an establishment or person under section 704 of the act, make each record and all information required to be collected and maintained under this part and all records and information related to the events and persons identified in such records available to FDA personnel. Any patient receiving a device subject to tracking requirements under this part may refuse to release, or refuse permission to release, the patient's name, address, telephone number, and social security number, or other identifying information for the purpose of tracking. Persons required to maintain records under this part shall maintain such records for the useful life of each tracked device they manufacture or distribute. The useful life of a device is the time a device is in use or in distribution for use. [1]

raw_model_output:
21 CFR Part 111 requires written procedures for quality control operations, including material review and disposition decisions, equipment, instruments, and controls, components, packaging, and labels, master manufacturing records, batch production records, and packaging and labeling operations, personnel qualification requirements, and returned dietary supplements. The requirements under this subpart include:

- Written procedures for quality control operations, as outlined in 21 CFR 111.103, 111.105, 111.10(a), 111.110, 111.113(a), 111.117, 111.120, 111.123(a), 111.127, 111.12(a), 111.130, 111.135, 111.13(a), and 111.140(a).  

- Personnel qualification requirements, as outlined in 21 CFR 111.140(a) and 111.14(a).  

- Records required under this subpart, including master manufacturing records, batch production records, and packaging and labeling operations, as outlined in 21 CFR 111.14(a).  

- Requirements for components, packaging, and labels before use, as outlined in 21 CFR 111.127.  

- Requirements for returned dietary supplements, as outlined in 21 CFR 111.135.  

- Requirements for product complaints, as outlined in 21 CFR 111.13(a).  

- Requirements for supervision of quality control operations, as outlined in 21 CFR 111.130.  

- Requirements for sanitation and ground maintenance, as outlined in 21 CFR 111.15(a).  

- Requirements for packaging and labels received, as outlined in 21 CFR 111.160(a).

raw_model_output: Under Part 111, the responsibilities of quality control personnel include ensuring the quality of dietary supplements through written procedures for conducting material reviews, making disposition decisions, and approving or rejecting reprocessing. Quality control personnel must also ensure the quality of the dietary supplement and packaging, labeling, and holding operations, including performing operations that involve material reviews and disposition decisions. They must prevent microbial contamination by excluding sick or infected personnel and implementing hygienic practices. raw_model_output: 21 CFR Part 820 Subpart Z requires manufacturers to establish and maintain a quality management system that is appropriate for their specific device(s). This system must ensure that finished devices are safe and effective and in compliance with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. If a manufacturer engages in only some operations subject to the requirements in this part, it must comply with those requirements applicable to the operations in which it is engaged. The requirements in this part apply to manufacturers that perform the functions of contract sterilization, installation, relabeling, remanufacturing, repacking, or specification development, as well as initial distributors of foreign entities that perform these functions.
